body.statement: There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class constants, such that along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\) and \(P\)-almost every \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\), \[cR_\star\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\le CR_\star.\] The raw feasible estimator in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} attains the upper bound with nonidentically distributed bounded event outcomes, an unknown heteroskedastic donor law, and estimated full \(\Sigma\).
body.justification: The theorem closes the joint-panel upper-and-lower frontier across arbitrary relative growth rates.
body.gap: Yan, Yao, and Zhou cover repeated-measurement prediction and Akhavan--Gogolashvili--Tsybakov cover an estimated strongly convex minimizer; neither has a causal joint law, a first-order external center, or a realized spacing barrier.
body.consumer: Empirical designers can determine whether adding donor securities, calendar windows, or cohort replications is the only way to reduce causal wealth risk.
